verdict.rationale: Codex supports natural-language-triggered skills and plugin commands (e.g. typing `$` to mention a skill, `/plugins` and `/skills` browsers, plugins like Slack/Gmail/Notion that respond to conversational requests like 'summarize channels'), suggesting a largely natural-language interaction model layered on slash-commands. However, core discovery/install still relies on explicit slash-commands (`/plugins`, `/skills`, `$skill-installer`) rather than pure freeform NL, and community feedback raises concerns about reliability of skill-based (text-instruction) invocation versus deterministic MCP tools. missing for 10: evidence of purely freeform NL invocation without slash-command/mention syntax, independent hands-on confirmation that NL commands reliably trigger correct plugin/skill without explicit naming.
